record.file_problem: The full post is present, but it is a linkpost summary; the linked research paper itself is not included.
record.tranche_reason: The post uses the toy model of features in superposition as a benchmark for APD and reports how well APD decomposes it. It does not report measurements testing the superposition geometry or its sparsity-dependent transition.
record.gate_note: The post reports a qualitative APD result on the toy model of features in superposition, recorded below as a result about the method's recovery of toy-model mechanisms. It does not report measurements of feature angles, sparsity thresholds, neuron polysemanticity, LLM features, or SAE features. The claims that APD can handle multidimensional features and cross-layer representations are not accompanied here by specific results on feature dimensionality.
record.test_reason: The post applies APD to the TMS toy model as a benchmark with known ground truth and reports only qualitatively how well APD recovers it. It reports no measurement of superposition geometry, sparsity transition, polysemanticity, LLM features, SAE features or feature dimensionality.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors find APD mostly works on toy models (TMS and compressed computation). They say it is brittle and hyperparameter-sensitive, shows some mechanism mixing, and is not yet usable on LLMs, but call the parameter-space approach promising.
record.recipe_differences: APD decomposes parameters into components using attribution-based selection and simplicity losses; it is not a reproduction of the original toy-model method.
record.method_sensitivity: The post says results required substantial hyperparameter tuning and attributes some mechanism mixing to the use of top-k.

fits_no_version.finding: APD largely decomposed the TMS model into components matching individual features in superposition, with some mechanism mixing and heavy hyperparameter tuning.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Parameter-space decomposition (APD) can recover per-feature weight components in a toy superposition model, imperfectly.

record.problems: The result is qualitative, with no numerical recovery metrics or uncertainty estimates stated in the post. The post itself reports substantial hyperparameter sensitivity and residual mechanism mixing. The linked paper is not included in the provided text.

untested.parts: No feature geometry, overlap or orthogonality, sparsity-dependent transition, or regular geometry is measured. TMS is used only as ground truth.
No results on causes of polysemanticity.
No LLM results. Scaling to LLMs is named only as future work.
No SAE feature tests. A commenter's argument that APD avoids feature splitting comes with no results.
Components can act on multi-dimensional features is stated as a design property. No result compares 1-D with multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: This is a linkpost summary; the underlying arXiv paper (2501.14926) is not in the text. The compressed-computation toy models (more computations than neurons) relate to computation in superposition, which is not one of the listed versions. No row is needed for them beyond the fits_no_version entry.

versions.untested_parts: No measured feature geometry, degree of overlap or orthogonality, sparsity-dependent transition, or regular geometry is reported.
No results about neuron polysemanticity, capacity pressure, or allocation of dedicated versus shared dimensions.
No results about polysemanticity or alternative causes of it.
No LLM neuron-spread or sparse-feature dictionary-recovery results.
No test of whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
The post mentions that APD components can represent multidimensional features, but reports no result comparing one-dimensional and multidimensional features.
